4. Appellant abjured his guilt and pleaded not guilty.

The prosecution examined prosecutrix "B" (PW-1) [name of prosecutrix has been masked in order to avoid her identity, although her name is mentioned in the deposition-sheet], father of the prosecutrix NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:26609 "A" (PW-2) [his name has been masked in order to avoid identity of the prosecutrix], mother of the prosecutrix "C" (PW-3) [her name has been masked in order to avoid identity of the prosecutrix], Cousin brother of the prosecutrix "D" (PW-4) [his name has been masked in order to avoid identity of the prosecutrix],
brother of the prosecutrix "E" (PW-5) [his name has been masked in order to avoid identity of the prosecutrix], Kadwa P Verma (PW-6), Dr. Vijay Kori (PW-7), Dr. Sandhya Swami (PW-8),
A.L.Tripathi (PW-9), Ashok Rao (PW-10), Kuber Singh (PW- 11).
6. Appellant did not examine any witness in his defence.
7. Trial Court by impugned judgment and sentence, convicted the appellant for the above-mentioned offences.
8.

Kadwa P Verma (PW-6) is the Headmaster of Government Primary School, Chandnipura,
Sanwad.

He has produced the scholar record of prosecutrix, according to which, prosecutrix was given admission in Class-1 on 4/7/2005 and according to the scholar register, date of birth of prosecutrix was mentioned as 13/11/1998 (Ex.P/6).
This witness was cross-
examined.
He admitted that he was posted in the school in the month of July, 2005 and the school register is not in his handwriting.
9. Prosecutrix "B" (PW-1) has stated that the appellant is not known to her.
She was all alone in the house.
At about 2 PM appellant came to her house and informed that health condition of her mother is not good and accordingly, she has called her.
Initially she refused to accompany him, but on his insistence, she went alongwith the appellant.
Appellant took her to Khargon in the house of his brother on a four wheeler.
She was unable to understand the things.

sentences.text: Thereafter, from Khargon appellant took her to Pithampur where he took a room on rent and when prosecutrix insisted that appellant should leave her in her house, then he extended a threat that he would kill her by strangulating her.
Her parents had lodged a Gum Insan report and accordingly, police contacted appellant on mobile and thereafter, appellant brought her back to Sanawad.
She informed the entire incident to her mother.
Her statement was recorded.

Thereafter,
she was sent for medical examination.
Her medical examination was conducted after obtaining consent of herself and her mother, which is Ex.P/1.
Her pubic hair, undergarment and vaginal slide was prepared by the doctor.
Recovery memo is Ex.P/2 was prepared.
Since she had not completely supported the prosecution case, therefore, she was declared partially hostile.
In cross-examination by the Public Prosecutor, she stated that she does not know the name of appellant, but she knows him from his face.
She further stated that she was insisting that appellant should leave her in her house and stated that she was taken to Pithampur.
She also denied that appellant took her to Mahu where she was raped by appellant.
She admitted that appellant had given a threat that he would kill her brother and because of that threat, she got afraid.
She admitted that only after extending a threat, he committed rape on her.
She was unable to disclose her date of birth, but stated that she is aged about 16 years.
She admitted that in her statement which was recorded before the Magistrate she has disclosed that the appellant had also raped her in Mahu.
In cross- examination, she stated that she has seen the appellant for the first time when he came and took her along with him.
She further stated that at the time of her kidnapping nobody else was present on the spot.
She further NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:26609 stated that she left the doors of her house opened while leaving the house.
Appellant had parked four wheeler Jeep behind her house.
Jeep was an open Jeep.
She further stated that Jeep had crossed police station as well as had passed through busy market.
However, she stated that she had requested appellant to take her to her mother.
She further stated that when they reached near Police Station Khargone, she had requested appellant to take her to her mother, but he did not stop the jeep.
She had requested him with higher voice.

She also stated that she had raised an alarm to inform general public that appellant is forcibly taking her, but appellant had extended a threat that in case if she raises alarm, then he would strangulate her.
This witness was not in a position to narrate the number of the jeep.
She was not in a position to disclose the location of the house situated in Khargone.
Appellant was driving the vehicle.
They came to Sanawad at about 1 PM.
They directly went to police station.
Her parents had also reached the police station.

She had tried to stop the appellant from committing Galat Kaam, however,
appellant had threatened that he would strangulate her, but she did not receive any injury.
She denied that she was aged about 19 years.
She denied that she had left the house without informing anybody and, therefore, Gum Insan report was lodged by her father.
She denied that at the instance of her father she is giving a false statement.

10. Evidence of prosecutrix is supported by evidence of father of the prosecutrix "A" (PW-2), mother of the prosecutrix "C" (PW-3), Cousin brother of the prosecutrix "D" (PW-4), brother of the prosecutrix "E" (PW-5) to whom the prosecutrix "B" (PW-1) had informed about the incident.

sentences.text: 11. Dr. Sandhya Swami (PW-8) had medically examined the prosecutrix.
She had prepared the vaginal swab and kept the same along with pubic hairs and undergarment in a sealed cover.
Her report is Ex.P- 8.
A.L. Tripathi (PW-9) is the Investigating Officer.
Ashok Rao (PW- 10) is the witness of recovery of prosecutrix.
Kuber Singh (PW-11) had seized the vaginal slide, pubic hair and undergarment of the prosecutrix from Constable Virendra vide seizure memo Ex.P-14.
The pubic hair, undergarment and slide of the appellant was also seized vide Ex.P-15.

FSL report has been received, according to which the semen stains and human sperms were found on underwear and semen slide of the appellant as well as on the underwear and vaginal slide of the prosecutrix.

12. Considering the totality of facts and circumstances of the case and in absence of any serious challenge to the age of prosecutrix and according to the scholar register, the date of birth of prosecutrix was 13/11/1998 and she was kidnapped on 12/02/2015, it is clear that the prosecutrix was less than 18 years and she was minor.
13. Accordingly, Trial Court did not commit any mistake by holding the appellant guilty for offence under Sections 363, 366, 376(1) of IPC and under Section 3/4 of POCSO Act.
14. The minimum sentence of 7 years was enhanced to 10 years by Act No.22 of 2018 and on the date of offence the minimum sentence for offence under Section 376(1) of IPC was 7 years.

Similarly,
for offence under Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, minimum sentence of 7 years was enhanced to 10 years by Act No.25/2019 and the minimum sentence for offence under Section 4 of POCSO Act was 7 years on the date of incident.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:26609 15.
Accordingly, sentence awarded by the Trial Court does not call for any interference.

16. Ex consequenti, judgment and sentence dated 15/09/2017 passed by Additional Sessions Judge,
Badwah, District Khargone in S.T. No.130/2015 is hereby affirmed.

Additional Sessions Judge,
Badwah, District Khargone
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 17. A PUD 10/08/2024 has been received from District Jail Khargone that the appellant after undergoing the entire jail sentence has been released on 15/09/2022.
Furthermore, it is clear from the order-sheets of this Court that the appellant was never granted bail.
18. In view of the PUD received from District Jail Khargone, it is clear that appellant has already undergone the entire jail sentence.
Accordingly, he is not required to surrender.
19. Copy of PUD dated 10/08/2024 be also annexed with this judgment for ready reference.
20. With aforesaid observations, appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.
